report:
## Conclusion

The claim that **giving children more vaccines causes more autism is not supported by credible scientific evidence**. It is understandable why the claim can seem plausible: autism signs often become noticeable during the same early-childhood period when many vaccines are given, and the childhood schedule has expanded. But timing or a population-level correlation cannot establish causation.

The directly relevant evidence is reassuring:

* A U.S. case-control study measured children’s *total exposure to vaccine antigens* (the immune-stimulating components), rather than merely counting shots. It found that greater cumulative antigen exposure in the first two years was **not associated with autism-spectrum disorder**.  
  https://www.jpeds.com/article/s0022-3476(13)00144-3/fulltext

* A very large nationwide Danish cohort study followed children and accounted for other childhood vaccines, sibling autism history, and known risk factors. It found **no increased autism risk from MMR**, including among children considered potentially more susceptible. This does not by itself test every possible schedule combination, but it strongly contradicts a major proposed vaccine-autism mechanism.  
  https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/30831578/

* A meta-analysis combining the available observational evidence likewise found no association between autism and vaccination, MMR, or thimerosal/mercury exposure.  
  https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/abs/pii/S0264410X14006367

* The National Academies’ review of safety concerns about the overall childhood schedule identified research gaps and recommended future study, but that is not evidence that schedule-related autism harm exists. “More study would be useful” is different from “the claim is established.”  
  https://www.nationalacademies.org/read/13563

In short, the evidence behind your sister’s view is chiefly temporal coincidence and hypothesis, not replicated evidence of causation. The studies designed to test higher vaccine/antigen exposure have not found an autism increase.
